sources.name: LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) 1m
facts: About 99% England coverage at 1 m resolution
Bare-earth DTM removes surface objects
Newest best-resolution repeat surveys are used
Resampling uses bilinear interpolation
sources.limit: Composite cells can come from different survey dates; source accuracy is not a parcel-specific confidence interval

sources.name: LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) 2m
facts: About 99% England coverage at 2 m resolution
Bare-earth surface semantics
Newest best-resolution data used where repeat surveys exist
Bilinear interpolation used during resampling
sources.limit: The 2 m layer is a QA crosscheck and cannot replace the pinned 1 m primary metric

sources.name: LIDAR DTM Time Stamped Tiles
facts: Survey-specific terrain archive
Supports explicit temporal lineage
Historic resolutions and transformation context must be retained
sources.limit: No historical tile may be numerically mixed without explicit survey-date and datum checks

sources.name: INSPIRE Index Polygons dataset
facts: Indicative extent and position of registered freehold properties
Files are separated by local authority
Each polygon has a unique Land Registry INSPIRE ID
Boundary polygons can appear in both authority files
sources.limit: The polygon is indicative and must not be represented as the legal title plan

sources.name: INSPIRE current download
facts: Current package published 5 July 2026
New files are published on the first Sunday of each month
Downloads are organised by local authority
Use is subject to Open Government Licence conditions
sources.limit: A local authority package remains current only until the next monthly publication

sources.name: Technical guidance for GML files
facts: Polygons are captured against British National Grid
Native CRS is EPSG:27700
Reprojection to web-map CRS is possible
BNG-to-WGS84 conversion can shift some features by up to 15 m
sources.limit: Exact containment and raster sampling must remain in native British National Grid

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 documentation
facts: Open height dataset for Great Britain
Updated annually in July
Grid has regular 50 m post spacing
Supplied in 10 km by 10 km National Grid tiles
sources.limit: Landscape-scale resolution is insufficient for primary sub-metre parcel measurement

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 technical specification
facts: Lower-resolution bare-earth DTM
Buildings and trees are removed from the terrain surface
Grid and contour forms share source data
Compressed folders contain data plus supporting files
sources.limit: The specification defines product structure, not correctness of a particular sampled value

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 grid data
facts: ASCII grid contains 200 rows by 200 columns
Pixels are 50 m by 50 m
Values are calculated from pixel centres
Heights are supplied to nearest 0.1 m
sources.limit: ASC/GML/PRJ structure must still be verified from the downloaded current archive bytes

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 metadata
facts: Per-tile XML follows GEMINI metadata standard
Metadata records spatial representation
Metadata includes 10 km tile reference
British National Grid is represented as EPSG:27700
sources.limit: Metadata cannot substitute for hashes of the outer archive, nested archive and raster files

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 GML feature types
facts: Terrain geometries use urn:ogc:def:crs:EPSG::27700
Feature and geometry identifiers are unique within a release
Height property is relative to Newlyn or another applicable British height datum
sources.limit: Release-specific IDs can be regenerated when a tile is refreshed

sources.name: Web Coverage Service standard
facts: WCS provides Internet access to multidimensional coverages
Core requirements are mandatory for conformant implementations
KVP, CRS, scaling, interpolation and encoding are separate extensions
WCS 2.0.1 core is an official implementation standard
sources.limit: A standard contract does not prove that a specific endpoint returned correct parcel values
